prompt: If I randomly select i.i.d. samples from a distribution n times, the distribution of the sampled variables will approximately follow a normal distribution as n becomes very large. This statement is based on which theory?
answer:
This statement is based on the **Central Limit Theorem (CLT)**—provided it refers to the distribution of the **sample means or sums**, not the individual observations.

If \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are i.i.d. with finite mean \(\mu\) and variance \(\sigma^2\), then as \(n\) becomes large,

\[
\frac{\sqrt n(\bar X-\mu)}{\sigma}\ \xrightarrow{d}\ N(0,1),
\]

so approximately,

\[
\bar X \sim N\left(\mu,\frac{\sigma^2}{n}\right).
\]

The individual sampled variables do **not** become normally distributed; their distribution remains the original population distribution. The **Law of Large Numbers** instead describes sample averages becoming close to \(\mu\).
